thread.title: Qualcomm Slapped With Antitrust Fine; TI Dips On Growth Concerns

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Qualcomm Slapped With Antitrust Fine; TI Dips On Growth Concerns
text:
Wireless-chip maker Qualcomm ( QCOM ) on Wednesday was fined the equivalent of $1.23 billion by the European Union for alleged anticompetitive behavior.
The EU's European Commission fined Qualcomm for abusing its market dominance in LTE baseband chip sets. The commission said Qualcomm prevented rivals from competing in the market by making significant payments to a key customer, Apple ( AAPL ), on condition it not buy from rivals, including Intel ( INTC ).
"Qualcomm illegally shut out rivals from the market for LTE baseband chip sets for over five years, thereby cementing its market dominance," Commissioner Margrethe Vestager said in a written statement . "Qualcomm paid billions of U.S. dollars to a key customer, Apple, so that it would not buy from rivals. These payments were not just reductions in price — they were made on the condition that Apple would exclusively use Qualcomm's baseband chip sets in all its iPhones and iPads."
Baseband chip sets enable smartphones and tablets to connect to cellular networks for voice and data transmission.
Qualcomm's actions are illegal under EU antitrust rules, Vestager said.

Qualcomm says it will appeal the European Commission's decision to the General Court of the European Union.
"We are confident this agreement did not violate EU competition rules or adversely affect market competition or European consumers," Don Rosenberg, executive vice president and general counsel of Qualcomm, said in a statement . "We have a strong case for judicial review and we will immediately commence that process."
Qualcomm shares slipped 0.5% to close at 67.98 on the stock market today .
Texas Instruments Falls On Sales Growth Concerns Texas Instruments stock fell Wednesday after the chipmaker posted its slowest revenue growth in four quarters on softer demand for its chips used in communications equipment.
TI shares tumbled 8.5% to close at 109.70 Wednesday.
Late Tuesday, TI reported December-quarter earnings that were in line with Wall Street's estimates, with sales slightly above views. It earned an adjusted $1.09 a share, up 24% year over year, on revenue of $3.75 billion, up 10%.
"For the first time in several quarters TI delivered merely an in-line quarter and guide, which for investors used to beat-and-raises may set up for a healthy pause (given the 20% plus move since last quarter)," Rosenblatt Securities analyst Hans Mosesmann said in a report. "The notion that TI can grow the top line at 10%-plus levels organically, as was the case in 2017, is simply untenable. However, 5-7% growth is we think a sweet spot for TI in terms of sales growth given its powerful position in analog/embedded markets where they are gaining dollar share on a secular basis."
Mosesmann reiterated his buy rating on TI stock and upped his price target to 135 from 120.
Texas Instruments stock received at least five price target increases on the news, as well as one decrease.
Microsemi Shares Rise On Takeover Speculation Chipmaker Microsemi ( MSCC ) has been approached about a possible takeover and is exploring its options, Reuters reported .
Microsemi has hired investment bank Qatalyst Partners to advise it on the best course of action, a source told Reuters.
Aliso Viejo, Calif.-based Microsemi is a major supplier of semiconductors for aerospace, defense, communications and industrial applications.
Microsemi stock climbed 1.8% to close at 63.44 on Wednesday. On Tuesday, Microsemi shares jumped 5.7% to end the day at 62.35.
